items.sefariaRef: Talmud Eser HaSefirot, Section XI, List of Answers on Terminology 7:1
items.html: All the Gadlut of ZA is included in the fillings of AB, SAG, MAH, which in Gematria are Kav [102] (see Answer 64). And through them come the vessels of NHY, which are his legs, and the GAR of the lights, as is known. And he attains this wholeness on the Sabbath day, for then he clothes AVI Ilain, and has all the lights in wholeness, as he had at the time of the Nekudim. But all this is only from the side of the lights alone; from the side of the vessels, however, he is considered in the standing of the ancient ZA of the Nekudim, who still lacks NHY of the vessels. For the ZA of the Nekudim was already whole even from the first Tzimtzum, and therefore expanded down to Assiya equally with the NHY of AK. This is not so with the ZA of Atzilut, who is cut off at the Parsa between Atzilut and Beria even on the Sabbath day, and whose legs do not reach the legs of AK. This is because the whole correction of the ZA of Atzilut is from the second Tzimtzum, from the secret of the joining of the quality of mercy with judgment, in the secret of ‘and the two of them went,’ where the two Heys are included one within the other. And from here come his fillings of AB, SAG, MAH, which are the Mochin of the Sabbath day. Therefore the Parsa beneath Atzilut remains in its full force even on the Sabbath, and he cannot expand into BYA equally with the legs of AK, as he will in the future, when his NHY will also be corrected from the aspect of the first Tzimtzum, and then his legs will reach the legs of AK, and it will be revealed in the secret of ‘and His feet shall stand upon the Mount of Olives,’ as is known.
